name: Conaniah
overview: Conaniah was a male Levite who served as an officer responsible for the consecrated things, indicating a significant role in the religious duties of Israel. His position underscores his entrusted responsibility within the Levitical service during the period described in 2 Chronicles. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond his official capacity.
namesAndTitles: The name Conaniah means "G-d has established?" according to the Hebrew meaning provided. This proper name reflects a recognition of God's sovereignty and establishment but was not specifically given by God as a direct revelation. The name appears in 2 Chronicles 31:12.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Conaniah as a descendant of Levi, placing him within the tribe set apart for priestly and temple service. He is also inferred to have a brother named Shimei, as noted in 2 Chronicles 31:13. Beyond these relationships, no other family connections are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Conaniah's significance lies in his leadership role over the consecrated things, highlighting his trusted position in managing sacred duties within the Levitical order. His service reflects the organized worship and dedication to God during the time of temple reforms and restoration. Through his role, Conaniah contributed to maintaining the holiness and proper administration of the temple services, which were vital for Israel's covenantal relationship with God.
